notes.text: Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and is unavailable to demo/shared accounts. The account must own the domain. Pre-flight failure is synchronous; detached failures appear later in operationStatus. Returning operationId establishes a submitted background operation, never a completed backup.

database is repeatable and omitted for a files-only archive; supplied list order and values are preserved without joining or JSON encoding. Database ownership is checked in the background, so an accepted request may later fail. A two-hour cap bounds the background work.
Omit email to send no notification. Supplying it requests best-effort mail on success or failure to that address; a ready status does not prove delivery. The client sends no notification itself.

All declared response fields are optional: omission stays distinct from zero, false, an empty string and explicit documented null. A missing or null data member is a payload mismatch. No general response-string enum or cross-field invariant validation is inferred.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and is unavailable to demo/shared accounts. This synchronous deletion removes named archives and sidecar manifests permanently. System-created backups are not user-deletable; the client provides no retry or rollback.

ids is repeatable and requires at least one non-empty value server-side. Empty ids produce no row; match results by id rather than position. A successful API envelope can contain mixed per-id ok=0 and ok=1 results, with error text for failures. Inspect every row. Flags remain integer 0/1.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and ownership of domain. This advisory estimate runs du over the document root with a one-hour timeout; avoid polling it on a timer. createBackup rechecks quota itself.

All byte amounts are integers. unlimited=1 makes availableBytes=0 mean not applicable; estimatedBytes=0 can mean the directory could not be measured, and then ok is also 1. The estimate excludes database dumps. ok and unlimited are payload integer 0/1 flags distinct from API success.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and is unavailable to demo/shared accounts. This detached operation copies archived website files and never overwrites existing destination files or activates the extracted site. It can run alongside another operation and has a two-hour cap. Returning operationId is submission, not completion; poll operationStatus.

id locates an archive in the selected account's backup directory and is not checked against domain. Use an id returned for the intended domain. path is server-side and relative to the account home; the server strips a leading slash and rejects .. segments but does not resolve home-directory symlinks. The client forwards it unchanged and uploads or downloads nothing.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and ownership of domain. Reads sidecar manifests for completed/existing archives and skips unreadable manifests; use listOperations for work in flight. Returned archive paths are server-side, not local downloads.

Rows default to newest createdMs first. createdMs is epoch milliseconds; sizeBytes is integer bytes. Empty databaseNames/sites lists remain lists and absent fields stay omitted. includesDatabases is an integer 0/1 flag. A source of system means the archive is not user-deletable.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and ownership of domain. Returns only still-running create, restore and extract operations; terminal and dead-daemon operations are omitted. An empty list alone does not establish success or failure.

Rows default to most recently updated first rather than start-time order. operationId can resume polling; extractPath is a server-side home-relative destination present for extraction only. startedAtMs is epoch milliseconds and progressPct remains numeric. Field omission is preserved and no cross-field presence constraints are inferred.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature. operationId identifies selected-account detached work. Poll until status differs from inProgress; ready and failed are terminal. UAPI status=1 means the status read succeeded and does not mean the background job succeeded.

The pinned kind/status strings are documented alternatives, not a closed runtime string enum. error, warnings, title and subStatus are returned payload text. Preserve optional warnings including an empty list; do not log returned upstream text as structural evidence. startedAtMs is epoch milliseconds and progressPct remains numeric.

Available in cPanel 138 and later; requires the selected account's backup feature and is unavailable to demo/shared accounts. This starts a destructive in-place restore, with a six-hour cap. Returning operationId is submission rather than completion; poll operationStatus and inspect errors and warnings. No automatic retry or rollback is added by the client.

Omitting clean uses a merge: archive files overwrite counterparts while newer files are retained. clean=1 selects a snapshot and removes files added since backup; clean=0 requests merge. This parameter is a pinned integer, not a boolean or the string false. The client preserves omitted defaults and explicit zero.

Omitting restoreDatabases restores archive databases by default. Send integer 0 to leave every database untouched; the string false is unsafe upstream because Perl treats it as true. Restored databases are reset to their backed-up state, dropping later objects. The server documents a rollback snapshot for a failed database restore; the client does not promise whole-site atomicity.

database is repeatable and selects an archive subset; omit it while restoring databases to restore them all. id is not checked against domain, so use a backup listed for the intended domain. Paths and archive identities stay server-side.
